\begin{definition}\label{def:compact}
A set is compact when every open cover has a finite subcover.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:closed}
A closed subset of a compact set is compact.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Assume hypothesis H. Then the image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take an open cover of the image and pull it back (see Lemma~\ref{lem:closed} and \cite{rudin}).
\end{proof}
